validation_obligations.title: Bounded instruction representation: only .b32 is representable
validation_obligations.description: The bounded unit fixes the mnemonic mov, the type specifier .b32, and the empty modifier set (the scalar mov syntax has no modifier position; PTX-MOV-SEM2-022). In Lean, MovTypeSpecifier has exactly one constructor .b32 and the type field is semantically inert (never read by execMovB32), so no other instruction type or modifier form can be represented or executed by this bounded mapping. Maps to architecture VAL-1 (type well-formedness: .b32 is a valid 32-bit bit-size fundamental type).

validation_obligations.title: B32 values are within the 32-bit .b32 domain by representation (PRF-6 disposition)
validation_obligations.description: Every B32 value wraps a Fin (2^32) value, so 0 <= toFin.val < 2^32 holds by construction for every value of type B32. This subsumes the future result-domain-membership topic PRF-6: any value produced by copyValue (in particular any value written to a destination register) is automatically in the 32-bit bit-size value domain of .b32; no deep theorem is needed beyond the representation invariant. This adopts the PRF-6 disposition recorded in semantics-v2 future_theorem_obligation_topics (semantic-critic v1 F-3): PRF-6 is reclassified as a definitional/validation-style well-formedness obligation (VAL-style, like VAL-1/VAL-2) rather than a semantic proof obligation, because under the typed register-file representation it would otherwise be vacuous. Maps to architecture VAL-1/VAL-2 style.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that the execution relation MovB32Step is deterministic: for any state s and instruction i, at most one resulting state is related. This is the derived determinism interpretation PTX-MOV-SEM2-039 (determinism NOT explicitly stated in the source, bundle GAP-2), realized non-vacuously over the relational semantics per design D-25 / PTX-MOV-SEM2-061. Because MovB32Step is a Prop-valued inductive relation and not a function, the theorem is not a definitional triviality: it must rule out the possibility that both the guardFalse and executed constructors (or two executions) relate distinct resulting states.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every machine state s, instruction i, and states s1, s2: if MovB32Step s i s1 and MovB32Step s i s2, then s1 = s2.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem movB32Step_deterministic
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s1 s2 : MachineState)
    (h1 : MovB32Step s i s1) (h2 : MovB32Step s i s2) :
    s1 = s2
hypotheses: h1 : MovB32Step s i s1 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s1)
h2 : MovB32Step s i s2 (the relation admits a step from s on i to s2)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s1 = s2 (at most one resulting state).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Derived interpretation PTX-MOV-SEM2-039 (determinism; GAP-2, not explicitly stated in the source); design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-061 (D-25 relational representation so that determinism is non-vacuous); design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-043 (two-case outcome executed/guardFalse). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-MOV-004 ('Write register d with the value of a.'), PTX-9.3-MOV-006 (Semantics 'd = a;'), PTX-9.3-MOV-021 (guard evaluation). No arithmetic-result assumption is involved because mov performs no arithmetic.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: The relation is inhabited: the executable example with r1 = 5 and unguarded mov.b32 r1, r1 (aliasing self-copy, demonstrated by #eval 5) yields a MovB32Step from the executed constructor; the @p with p = false example (r1 stays 5) yields a MovB32Step from the guardFalse constructor. The conclusion s1 = s2 is not an element of the hypotheses; the theorem excludes a hypothetical relation that admitted two distinct results. This is the meaningful relational determinism property required by D-25; the trivial single-valuedness of the total function execMovB32 is NOT this obligation (see traceability_summary.determinism_note).
strength_risks: The theorem must not be misread as functional totality of execMovB32; it is a relational property over MovB32Step only.

The proof is a short case analysis on the two constructors using disjointness of evalGuard outcomes (some false vs some true) and is appropriate; the reviewer should confirm the statement adds no unapproved totality or totality-on-well-formed-domain precondition.
The theorem does not assert existence of a step (that is a completeness/correspondence matter, PTX-MOV-THM-002); it asserts uniqueness when a step exists.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on h1 and h2. If both come from the guardFalse constructor, the conclusion is reflexivity (s1 = s and s2 = s). If both come from the executed constructor, both give the same post-state updateDestination s i.d (copyValue va) with (possibly) different va values, but each constructor premise fixes evalSource s i.a to the respective va, so injectivity of some (Option) yields va1 = va2. If one is guardFalse and the other executed, the premises force evalGuard s i.guard = some false and evalGuard s i.guard = some true respectively, contradicting the disjointness of the two Option Bool values; derive False.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 (determinism of the execution relation).

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the correspondence between the executable function execMovB32 and the relational semantics MovB32Step. This is the item explicitly deferred by the Lean mapping critic (lean-mapping-critic-v1 F-4: 'the relational form and the executable function are both present, but their correspondence is unproven and explicitly deferred (PRF-1 family)'). The correspondence has four parts: (a)-(b) soundness (every outcome of the function is a step), (c) completeness (every step is realized by some function outcome), and (d) partial-completeness (function partiality none occurs exactly when the relation admits no step). Part (d) makes the partial-execution convention (Option none = partial execution for out-of-domain states, not an error; PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042/043) precise with respect to the relation.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) If execMovB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.executed s'), then MovB32Step s i s'. (b) If execMovB32 s i returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'), then MovB32Step s i s'. (c) If MovB32Step s i s', then there exists an outcome o with execMovB32 s i = some o and o is either ExecOutcome.executed s' or ExecOutcome.guardFalse s'. (d) execMovB32 s i = none if and only if there is no state s' with MovB32Step s i s'.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem exec_sound_executed
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) :
    MovB32Step s i s'

theorem exec_sound_guardFalse
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')) :
    MovB32Step s i s'

theorem step_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (h : MovB32Step s i s') :
    Exists fun (o : ExecOutcome) =>
      execMovB32 s i = some o /\
      (o = ExecOutcome.executed s' \/ o = ExecOutcome.guardFalse s')

theorem step_partial_complete
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) :
    execMovB32 s i = none <->
      not (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) => MovB32Step s i s')
hypotheses: Parts (a), (b), (d) quantify over arbitrary states and instructions; no additional preconditions are added.
Part (c) takes h : MovB32Step s i s' and concludes the existence of a corresponding function outcome.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: The four stated equivalences/implications between execMovB32 and MovB32Step.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: Design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-061 (D-25 relational representation; relation/function correspondence is a theorem-stage obligation in the PRF-1 family); design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-043 (two-case outcome, no error constructor); DERIVED guard behavior PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038 (guard-false no-op) and PTX-MOV-SEM2-035/037 (copy rule and guard-true behavior). Partiality convention PTX-MOV-SEM2-041 (no invented error/UB; Option none is partial execution). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-MOV-004, PTX-9.3-MOV-006, PTX-9.3-MOV-035, PTX-9.3-MOV-036.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable witnesses for every part exist among the executable examples: part (b) via the @p with p = false example (guardFalse outcome; also a guardFalse step), part (a) via the aliasing self-copy example (executed outcome; also an executed step), part (c) via both of those steps, and part (d) via the partial-execution example (missing source register yields none and no step). The conclusions are not elements of the hypotheses; each direction requires unfolding the definitions of both the function and the relation and is the substantive bridge deferred by mapping-critic F-4.
strength_risks: Part (d) must not be misread as asserting totality over all states; none for out-of-domain states is partiality (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042/043; risk R-2).

The relation omits the none partial case (it relates only complete executions); this is a mapping decision consistent with D-25 (mapping-critic F-4) and the correspondence makes it precise rather than hiding it.
The reviewer should confirm the four statements add no unapproved preconditions and use exactly the constructors of ExecOutcome.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: All four parts unfold execMovB32 and MovB32Step and case-split on evalGuard (Option Bool: none/some false/some true) and, where the executed branch is reached, on evalSource (Option B32). Part (a): with h, the evalGuard match took the some true branch and evalSource the some va branch; instantiate the executed constructor. Part (b): the evalGuard match took the some false branch; instantiate the guardFalse constructor (note ExecOutcome.guardFalse s' forces s' = s). Part (c): case on the step constructor; for guardFalse, hguard : evalGuard = some false gives the guardFalse outcome; for executed, hguard and hsource give the executed outcome with o = ExecOutcome.executed s'. Part (d): forward by cases on evalGuard/evalSource; reverse by showing each constructor would contradict execMovB32 = none.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-1 family (determinism and relation/function correspondence); mapping-critic F-4.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the copy-fidelity property: when the guard is true, the destination is a register r, and the source resolves in the pre-instruction state s, the value written to r equals the value read from the source. This is the Semantics line 'd = a;' (PTX-9.3-MOV-006; SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-035) and the derived copy rule PTX-MOV-SEM2-036 (a bit-for-bit copy of the 32-bit untyped .b32 value; no arithmetic, conversion, or truncation). Because the source value is read from the pre-instruction state s (not from any post-update state), the statement also subsumes the read-before-write aliasing behavior PTX-MOV-SEM2-062: when i.a = SourceOperand.reg r (d aliases a), the value va is the pre-update value of r, and the destination keeps that same value. The exact formal statement is the semantic-phase matter OQ-9 / PTX-MOV-SEM2-068; this is the proposed formalization for theorem-strength review.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, register r, and B32 value va: if the complete guard expression evaluates true in s, i.d is the register destination r, and evalSource s i.a = some va (the source resolves in the pre-instruction state s with value va), then execMovB32 s i returns the executed outcome with some post-state s' and s'.valueRegs r = some va. The equality pins the written value to the value read from the pre-instruction state, which is exactly the copy rule and the read-before-write aliasing behavior.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execMovB32_copy_fidelity
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (r : RegId) (va : B32)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true)
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r)
    (ha : evalSource s i.a = some va) :
    Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
      execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\
      s'.valueRegs r = some va
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some true (the complete guard expression is true, including the unguarded case)
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r; the bit-bucket destination is handled by PTX-MOV-THM-005)
ha : evalSource s i.a = some va (the source resolves in the pre-instruction state s; va is the pre-update value)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: Exists s' : MachineState, execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s') /\ s'.valueRegs r = some va, i.e. the value written to r equals the value read from the source.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-035 (Semantics 'd = a;', PTX-9.3-MOV-006); DERIVED copy rule PTX-MOV-SEM2-036 (bit-for-bit copy of the 32-bit untyped .b32 value; grounded in PTX-9.3-MOV-004/006/024/026); DERIVED source read PTX-MOV-SEM2-030; DERIVED destination write PTX-MOV-SEM2-032; DERIVED read-before-write PTX-MOV-SEM2-062; OPEN_QUESTION PTX-MOV-SEM2-068 (OQ-9: exact Lean statement of the copy-fidelity candidate obligation PRF-7).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example mov.b32 r1, imm 7 (r1 becomes 7) and the aliasing self-copy example mov.b32 r1, r1 with r1 = 5 (r1 stays 5). The conclusion (the written value is exactly the read value va) is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the destination write to the pre-state source read and distinguishes copy semantics from any transformation, truncation, or read-after-write semantics.
strength_risks: The equality s'.valueRegs r = some va relies on copyValue being the identity (the copy rule d = a; PTX-MOV-SEM2-035/036). If copyValue were ever changed to a non-identity, the statement would need to become s'.valueRegs r = some (copyValue va); the reviewer should keep this dependency explicit.
The theorem must keep va defined from the pre-instruction state s (never from the post-state s'), or the read-before-write content (PTX-MOV-SEM2-062) would be lost.
The theorem does not assert behavior for missing registers; those are out-of-domain partiality (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042; risk R-2).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execMovB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some true branch; with ha the evalSource match selects some va; the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed (updateDestination s i.d (copyValue va))). With hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination and simplify the valueRegs update function (fun r' => if r' == r then some (copyValue va) else s.valueRegs r') with the DecidableEq of RegId to conclude s'.valueRegs r = some (copyValue va); since copyValue va = va by definition, conclude some va. The aliasing case i.a = SourceOperand.reg r follows with ha : evalSource s (SourceOperand.reg r) = some va and evalSource unfolding to s.valueRegs r = some va, i.e. the pre-update value.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-7 (copy fidelity: the value written equals the value read, 'd = a;', PTX-9.3-MOV-006); read-before-write aspect of PTX-MOV-SEM2-062.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the destination-only update / frame property over the execution relation: when a step executes with a register destination r, the only value register that may change is r; every other value register and every predicate register is unchanged. This is the relational frame obligation (architecture PRF-2; semantics future topic PRF-2) grounded in DERIVED claims PTX-MOV-SEM2-032 (only the destination register is updated) and PTX-MOV-SEM2-033 (write locality: no memory, special-register, carry-flag, status-register, or condition-code component is written by the bounded base mov.b32). The statement is made over the bounded model (value-register file plus predicate-register file) and retains the documented negative-evidence caveat: the bounded model contains no carry-flag/status components, and the absence of such writes is absence-based negative evidence (PTX-MOV-SEM2-033/041/042; mapping-critic F-1; risk R-1), not an affirmative NVIDIA enumeration; the frame claim must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, related state s', and register r: if MovB32Step s i s' and i.d is the register destination r, then (1) every value register r' different from r has the same value in s' as in s; and (2) every predicate register p has the same value in s' as in s. The theorem holds in both the executed and the guard-false cases (in the guard-false case s' = s, so the frame is trivially satisfied; the executed case is the content).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem movB32Step_destination_only_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState) (r : RegId)
    (hstep : MovB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.reg r) :
    (forall (r' : RegId), r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\
    (forall (p : PredId), s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p)
hypotheses: hstep : MovB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.reg r (the destination is the register r)
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (forall r', r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r') /\ (forall p, s'.predRegs p = s.predRegs p).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED claims PTX-MOV-SEM2-032 (state write: destination register d updated with the value of a; the source states no other register write) and PTX-MOV-SEM2-033 (write locality: only the destination update required by the bounded semantics; no memory/special-register/carry/status component written); PTX-MOV-SEM2-058 (minimal state pair). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-MOV-003, PTX-9.3-MOV-004, PTX-9.3-MOV-006. The absence of carry/status writes is NEGATIVE evidence (PTX-MOV-SEM2-033/041/042; mapping-critic F-1; risk R-1).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with r1 = 1, r2 = 2 and updateDestination (Destination.reg r1) (mkB32 100) shows r1 becomes 100 while r2 remains 2 and the predicate file is untouched. The conclusion (all other value registers and all predicates preserved) is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the frame content and distinguishes destination-only semantics from any semantics writing additional state.
strength_risks: Risk R-1 (mapping-critic F-1; PTX-MOV-SEM2-033/041/042): the theorem must be stated over the bounded model only and must not be cited as an explicit NVIDIA statement that 'no carry flag / status register is written'. The absence-based caveat must remain traceable until final acceptance.

The theorem does not assert the value written to r itself (that is PTX-MOV-THM-003); a reviewer should ensure no attempt to strengthen this theorem into an assertion about components outside the model.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s, so both conjuncts are by reflexivity. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (copyValue va); with hd : i.d = Destination.reg r, unfold updateDestination: the valueRegs function becomes fun r' => if r' == r then some (copyValue va) else s.valueRegs r'. Use by_cases (r' == r) on the DecidableEq of RegId to prove r' != r -> s'.valueRegs r' = s.valueRegs r'; predicate registers are untouched because only the valueRegs field is updated in the record (predRegs equality by record simplification).
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-2 (destination-only update / frame), with negative-evidence caveat from risk R-1.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the bit-bucket discard property over the execution relation: when the destination is the bit bucket '_', a step changes no value register and the whole state is unchanged (s' = s). This corresponds to semantics future topic PRF-3. The obligation retains the documented strength caveat: the no-write consequence is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-015 / fragment PTX-9.3-MOV-019; open question PTX-MOV-SEM2-047/AMB-3, bundle GAP-6); the scalar mov.b32 section does not demonstrate the bit-bucket form, so the theorem must not be presented as a mov.b32-specific explicit source fact (mapping-critic F-1).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s, instruction i, and related state s': if MovB32Step s i s' and i.d is the bit bucket Destination.bitBucket, then s' = s: the computed value is discarded and no value register or predicate register changes. The strength of this claim is limited to the general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule (PTX-MOV-SEM2-015/047).
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem movB32Step_bit_bucket_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : MovB32Step s i s')
    (hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hstep : MovB32Step s i s' (the relation admits a step from s on i to s')
hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket (the destination is the bit bucket '_')
theorem_obligations.conclusion: s' = s (the related state is exactly the input state; the result is discarded).
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-015 (general section 9.2 bit-bucket rule: for some instructions a bit bucket '_' may be used in place of a destination register; PTX-9.3-MOV-019); OPEN_QUESTION PTX-MOV-SEM2-047 (whether '_' is permitted for the scalar mov.b32 value-copy form; AMB-3, GAP-6); design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-043 (execution outcome representation).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: the executable example with the bit bucket destination keeps r1 at 1 (no value register written), demonstrating the no-write behavior; a guard-false step with bit bucket destination also satisfies s' = s. The conclusion s' = s is not an element of the hypotheses; it is the discard content and distinguishes the bit-bucket destination from the register destination (PTX-MOV-THM-003/004).
strength_risks: Risk R-3 (AMB-3 / PTX-MOV-SEM2-047 / mapping-critic F-1): the theorem must not be presented as mov.b32-specific explicit NVIDIA behavior; it is supported only to the strength of the general section 9.2 rule. PRF-3 strength must not exceed this.

If the theorem-strength review decides the bit-bucket constructor should be deferred until the scalar applicability question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-047) is resolved, this obligation is removed or weakened accordingly; the current statement is faithful to the Gate-C-approved Lean mapping, which materializes the constructor at candidate strength (mapping-critic F-1).
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Case on hstep. The guardFalse constructor gives s' = s directly. The executed constructor gives s' = updateDestination s i.d (copyValue va); with hd : i.d = Destination.bitBucket, unfold updateDestination: the bitBucket branch returns s, so s' = s; simp.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-3 (bit-bucket discard), with AMB-3 strength caveat.

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish that when the complete guard expression evaluates false, the instruction is not executed and the machine state is unchanged. This is the guard-false frame property (semantics future topic PRF-4), grounded in the DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038, which is source-resolved via the official section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036; SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-072/073; derivation chain PTX-MOV-SEM2-076). It is NOT a human assumption and must never be presented as one. The functional form (a) states that the guard-false outcome carries exactly the input state, so no value-register or predicate-register component changes; it also entails that source operands are NOT read in this branch (the code returns before evaluating sources), matching the mapping decision noted by mapping-critic F-2 and supported by the official @!p div.f32 division-by-zero example (PTX-9.3-MOV-037). The relational form (b) states the same over MovB32Step.
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: (a) For every state s and instruction i, if evaluating the complete guard expression in s yields some false, then execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s): the outcome is the guard-false outcome carrying exactly the input state, so no machine-state component changes and no source operand is read. (b) For every state s, instruction i, and related state s', if MovB32Step s i s' and evalGuard s i.guard = some false, then s' = s.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem execMovB32_guard_false_preserves_state
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s)

theorem movB32Step_guard_false_frame
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (s' : MachineState)
    (hstep : MovB32Step s i s')
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false) :
    s' = s
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some false (the complete guard expression evaluates false in s)
No source-resolution hypotheses are needed: the guard-false branch does not read source operands (this is part of the conclusion, not a precondition; mapping-critic F-2).
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (a) execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s); consequently the carried state equals the input state and the instruction has no state effect. (b) MovB32Step s i s' with evalGuard = some false forces s' = s.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: DERIVED_INTERPRETATION PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038 (guard-false no-op), source-resolved via SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-072/073 (section 9.7.13.2 clause 'Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' and Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction', PTX-9.3-MOV-035/036) and the derivation chain PTX-MOV-SEM2-076; design dependency PTX-MOV-SEM2-043 (two-case outcome, guardFalse carries the unchanged state). Source-non-reading in the guard-false branch is a mapping decision (mapping-critic F-2) supported by the official @!p div.f32 division-by-zero example (PTX-9.3-MOV-037).
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Satisfiable hypotheses: any state in which the referenced guard predicate is defined to false, or @!p with p true (the executable example @p with p = false keeps r1 at 5 demonstrates the behavior). The conclusion is not an element of the hypotheses; it pins the exact outcome constructor and the unchanged carried state, which is the semantic content of 'do nothing'.
strength_risks: The guard-false behavior must be presented as a DERIVED_INTERPRETATION from the explicit predication clause applied to mov.b32 (PTX-MOV-SEM2-034/038/076), never as an affirmative per-instruction SOURCE_FACT that the PTX mov section itself states this.
The theorem is stated over the bounded model state pair; it does not by itself assert anything about components outside the model (deferred property PTX-MOV-DEF-001).

Part (a)'s equality to ExecOutcome.guardFalse s (carrying exactly s) is a full state-preservation statement because guardFalse carries the whole MachineState and the only producer of guardFalse in execMovB32 is the unchanged input state.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Part (a): unfold execMovB32; with hguard the evalGuard match selects the some false branch, which returns some (ExecOutcome.guardFalse s) directly; the source-evaluation branch is never reached, so no source-resolution case analysis is needed. Part (b): case on hstep; the executed constructor requires evalGuard = some true, which contradicts hguard (injectivity of some on Option Bool), so only the guardFalse constructor applies and s' = s.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-4 (guard-false frame); mapping-critic F-2 (source-non-reading decision).

theorem_obligations.intent: Establish the guard-behavior equivalence (semantics future topic PRF-5): on the approved well-formed lookup domain, an executed outcome occurs if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. This covers the no-guard, @p, and @!p cases uniformly through evalGuard and pins the outcome classification of execMovB32. It complements PTX-MOV-THM-006 (guard-false state preservation) by providing the reverse direction: an executed outcome implies the guard was true, so an instruction can never execute under a false complete guard. The supporting guard-evaluation lemmas pin the per-constructor behavior of evalGuard (unguarded = true; @p = predicate value; @!p = negation) per PTX-MOV-SEM2-009/027/031 and the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (PTX-MOV-SEM2-073).
theorem_obligations.precise_statement_in_words: For every state s and instruction i, if the complete guard expression resolves in s to some b and, when b is true, the source resolves in s, then there exists an executed outcome from execMovB32 s i if and only if b is true. Equivalently: execution happens exactly when the complete guard expression is true; when b is false the outcome is the guard-false outcome (and, by PTX-MOV-THM-006, the state is unchanged). Supporting lemmas: evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true; s.predRegs p = some false -> evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false; s.predRegs p = some true -> evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false.
theorem_obligations.lean_statement_sketch:
theorem movB32_executes_iff_guard_true
    (s : MachineState) (i : MovB32Instruction) (b : Bool)
    (hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b)
    (hsources : b = true -> Exists fun (va : B32) => evalSource s i.a = some va) :
    (Exists fun (s' : MachineState) =>
        execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true

-- supporting guard-evaluation lemmas (per-constructor evalGuard behavior)
theorem evalGuard_unguarded_true
    (s : MachineState) : evalGuard s Guard.unguarded = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_true_when_pred_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some true

theorem evalGuard_atPos_false
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some false) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atPos p) = some false

theorem evalGuard_atNeg_false_when_pred_true
    (s : MachineState) (p : PredId) (h : s.predRegs p = some true) :
    evalGuard s (Guard.atNeg p) = some false
hypotheses: hguard : evalGuard s i.guard = some b (the complete guard expression resolves in s to b)
hsources : if b = true then the source resolves in s: Exists va, evalSource s i.a = some va
No additional guard or source preconditions.
theorem_obligations.conclusion: (Exists s', execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s')) <-> b = true; plus the per-constructor evalGuard lemmas.
theorem_obligations.source_or_assumption_basis: SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-009 (optional guard predicate @{!}p; instructions without a guard execute unconditionally); DERIVED PTX-MOV-SEM2-027 (guard well-typedness) and PTX-MOV-SEM2-031 (guard predicate read); DERIVED PTX-MOV-SEM2-037 (guard-true behavior); SOURCE_FACT PTX-MOV-SEM2-073 (general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction', PTX-9.3-MOV-036). Source evidence: PTX-9.3-MOV-016, PTX-9.3-MOV-021, PTX-9.3-MOV-022, PTX-9.3-MOV-035, PTX-9.3-MOV-036, PTX-9.3-MOV-037.
theorem_obligations.non_vacuity_argument: Both directions are non-trivial. Forward: with b = true and hsources, the code reaches the executed branch. Reverse: with b = false, the code returns guardFalse, so no executed outcome exists. There exist states satisfying the hypotheses for both values of b (e.g., @p with p true and with p false), and the theorem's biconditional is false if the outcome classification were wrong, so it is not vacuous. The supporting evalGuard lemmas pin the per-constructor guard evaluation and distinguish @p from @!p (opposite execution conditions; PTX-MOV-SEM2-009/027/031).
strength_risks: The theorem is a classification/guard-behavior statement, not a determinism claim; it must not be mistaken for PRF-1 (relational determinism, PTX-MOV-THM-001) or for the functional single-valuedness of execMovB32.

The hypothesis shape must match the well-formed lookup domain exactly; adding source-resolution hypotheses unconditionally (even when b = false) would be an unapproved strengthening and would make the reverse direction trivial in a different way.
The supporting lemmas are simple definitional statements; they must not be presented as deep semantic theorems, only as the per-constructor guard evaluation facts behind PRF-5.
theorem_obligations.proof_strategy_hint: Unfold execMovB32. Forward direction: assume b = true, use hsources to obtain va; evalGuard gives some true, evalSource gives some va, so the result is some (ExecOutcome.executed _). Reverse direction: assume Exists s', execMovB32 s i = some (ExecOutcome.executed s'); the evalGuard match in execMovB32 must have taken the some true branch (the some false branch returns guardFalse and the none branch returns none), hence b = true (use hguard and injectivity of some). The supporting lemmas unfold evalGuard and evaluate the match on the constructor.
theorem_obligations.proof_obligation_topic_reference: Semantics future topic PRF-5 (guard behavior: executes iff complete guard expression true, covering no-guard, @p, @!p uniformly).

deferred_properties.title: Whole-PTX frame claims about components outside the minimal state (carry flags, status/condition-code registers, memory, shared, special registers)
deferred_properties.description: The bounded model is the minimal approved pair (value-register file, predicate-register file). Statements such as 'mov.b32 writes no carry flag or status register' are absence-based negative evidence (PTX-MOV-SEM2-033/041/042; mapping-critic F-1; risk R-1), not affirmative NVIDIA enumeration. No theorem is proposed over components outside the bounded model; PTX-MOV-THM-004 is stated strictly over the model and retains the caveat.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Requires a broader machine model outside this bounded unit; negative evidence must not be presented as an affirmative theorem.

deferred_properties.title: Scalar mov.b32-specific bit-bucket demonstration (PTX-MOV-SEM2-047 / AMB-3)
deferred_properties.description: PTX-MOV-THM-005 states the no-write consequence at the strength of the general section 9.2 rule (PTX-MOV-SEM2-015/047). Whether the scalar mov.b32 section itself demonstrates the bit-bucket form remains an open question (AMB-3, GAP-6; mapping-critic F-1). Strengthening the bit-bucket theorem into an explicit mov.b32-specific source claim is deferred pending official evidence.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-MOV-SEM2-047; scalar mov.b32-specific demonstration absent.

deferred_properties.title: Constant-immediate range/encoding well-formedness (PTX-MOV-SEM2-048 / AMB-4)
deferred_properties.description: The allowed range and encoding of constant immediate source operands is not stated in the evidence (PTX-MOV-SEM2-048/067, bundle GAP-5, AMB-4). This affects static well-formedness of programs only and does not change the state transition of a given legal instruction. Any theorem about which immediates are legal is deferred.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-MOV-SEM2-048; static well-formedness, outside executable-semantics scope.

deferred_properties.title: Version and target gating theorems (PTX-MOV-SEM2-028/044/045/046)
deferred_properties.description: Base mov (and therefore the bounded base mov.b32 form) is introduced in PTX ISA 1.0 (PTX-MOV-SEM2-028/044); no family-specific target restriction is stated for the scalar mov.b32 register/immediate value-copy form in the scalar section read (PTX-MOV-SEM2-045), and the scalar base form's target set is an open question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-046). These are static validation-layer obligations (architecture VAL-5/VAL-6), not executable state-transition behavior; the Lean candidate does not model version/target metadata. Theorems about version/target validity are deferred to the validation layer.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Version/target metadata is outside the executable mapping scope of the bounded unit.

deferred_properties.title: Behavior on out-of-domain states (missing guard predicate or source register)
deferred_properties.description: For states in which a referenced guard predicate or source register is not defined, execMovB32 returns none. This is PARTIAL execution for out-of-domain states, not an error, trap, undefined behavior, or implementation-defined behavior (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042/043; mapping-critic F-2; risk R-2). No theorem will be stated about 'error' behavior, and none must never be interpreted as an approved error. The partial-completeness correspondence (PTX-MOV-THM-002 part (d)) makes this convention precise: none occurs exactly when the relation admits no step.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: The approved semantics fixes behavior only for the well-formed domain; out-of-domain behavior is a partiality convention, not a semantic property.

deferred_properties.title: Error / undefined / implementation-defined behavior claims (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042)
deferred_properties.description: No explicit error, trap, undefined-behavior, or implementation-defined-behavior clause for mov (or mov.b32) was found in the evidence (bundle GAP-3); none is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is an open question (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042). Any future claim of such behavior requires official evidence and is deferred.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Absence of evidence; no behavior invented; any positive claim would require new official evidence.

deferred_properties.title: Predicate register value-domain encoding (PTX-MOV-SEM2-069 / OQ-5)
deferred_properties.description: The exact Lean encoding of the 1-bit predicate register value domain (predicate registers are 1-bit, PTX-9.3-MOV-026) is a Lean-mapping decision for a later phase (PTX-MOV-SEM2-069/OQ-5). The Lean candidate uses Bool for predicate values (design D-13); the encoding decision itself is not a theorem obligation. If the encoding changes, the guard-evaluation lemmas in PTX-MOV-THM-007 must be re-verified against the new encoding.
deferred_properties.reason_deferred: Open question PTX-MOV-SEM2-069; encoding is a Lean-mapping decision, not a semantic property.

known_risks.description: Negative-evidence caveat for the frame/no-carry statements (mapping-critic F-1; PTX-MOV-SEM2-033/041/042). PTX-MOV-THM-004 and any frame reasoning must be stated over the bounded model and must not cite 'no carry flag / status register is written' as an explicit NVIDIA statement. Caveat retained in PTX-MOV-THM-004 and deferred property PTX-MOV-DEF-001; must remain traceable until final acceptance.

Option none is partiality, not an error (PTX-MOV-SEM2-041/042/043; mapping-critic F-2). All faithfulness theorems quantify over the approved well-formed lookup domain via lookup-success hypotheses (PTX-MOV-THM-003/007 shape); none must never be interpreted as an approved error/trap/UB behavior.

Bit-bucket strength is limited to the general section 9.2 rule (AMB-3 / PTX-MOV-SEM2-047 / mapping-critic F-1). PTX-MOV-THM-005 retains the strength caveat and is not presented as mov.b32-specific explicit behavior.
Constant-immediate range/encoding remains open (PTX-MOV-SEM2-048/067). Affects static well-formedness only; deferred property PTX-MOV-DEF-003.

Theorem statements in this specification are Lean sketches, not compiled Lean. Independent theorem-strength review (Gate THEOREM_STRENGTH) must validate each statement's hypotheses, non-vacuity, and faithfulness before any proof file is written.
